points.quote: **Headless plugin host.** Headless plugins get one shared backend host process. ... Theia plugins are handled in ... VS Code extensions are handled in `plugin-ext-vscode/src/node/plugin-vscode-init.ts`.

They run in an isolated host ... For each connected frontend, the Theia backend forks a separate Node process to host that frontend's plugins. ... Browser-side plugins run in a web worker ... **Ext** is the code in the plugin host. It can't use Theia's services.

The API is declared in `packages/plugin/src/theia.d.ts`. `createAPIFactory` in `packages/plugin-ext/src/plugin/plugin-context.ts` builds the implementation. ... VS Code extensions are handled in `plugin-ext-vscode/src/node/plugin-vscode-init.ts`. It reuses the Theia API and overrides a few members.
In Node, module loading is overridden so that `import 'vscode'` or `import '@theia/plugin'` returns that object. ... In a web worker, the API is assigned to `window['theia']`.

Each side holds a proxy to the other, built from a paired interface. Pairs include `LanguagesMain` and `LanguagesExt` in `plugin-ext/src/common/plugin-api-rpc.ts`. Methods that can be called over RPC start with `$`.
For each connected frontend, the Theia backend forks a separate Node process to host that frontend's plugins. ... In the normal (non-headless) case the Theia backend only relays the messages.

Functions and object references can't. For those, the creating side caches the object and sends a handle (an id), and the other side uses the handle to call back in. Messages are encoded with msgpackr.

Headless plugins get one shared backend host process. It isn't tied to any frontend. ... **Main** is the code in the browser frontend, or in the Node backend for headless plugins. ... They only see custom APIs that the application or other headless plugins contribute.
